title: Software Development Engineer II (Backend)
description:
**About GoKwik**
GoKwik is a growth operating system for D2C and eCommerce brands, enabling checkout optimization, RTO reduction, payments, retention, and post-purchase engagement. Today, GoKwik powers 15,000+ merchants globally, processes ~$2 billion in GMV, and continues to strengthen its AI-powered infrastructure across India, the UK, Europe, and the US.
  
  
**Why This Role Matters**
As an SDE 2 on the App Store & Developer Platform, you will own the system third-party developers build against and merchants install apps from. That covers OAuth and token lifecycle, app registration, scoped permissions, install and uninstall flows, webhook delivery and the public API contract developers depend on. Increasingly, it also means making the platform safe for AI agents and AI-built apps to use.
  
  
Our platform is multi-tenant: one system serves many merchants, each with its own catalogue, orders, inventory, pricing and customers, and it handles millions of API calls every week. This is production engineering, not greenfield prototyping. The services you join already carry live traffic, real merchant data and third-party integrations that cannot break.
  
  
The defining constraint of this role is that your API is somebody else's production dependency. A breaking change is not a deploy you can roll back quietly; it is an outage in someone else's product. You will own designs for your area, make decisions other engineers build on, run your services in production, and mentor SDE 1 engineers.
  
  
**What You'll Own**

* Design & Delivery - Own the design and delivery of app-store and developer-platform services: write low-level and high-level designs, decide on APIs, data models and failure handling, and document the reasoning.
* OAuth & Token Lifecycle - Own OAuth 2.0 flows end to end: authorisation code with PKCE, refresh and rotation, revocation, scope enforcement and the failure modes of each.
* Public APIs - Build and version public APIs that external developers integrate against, with deprecation paths, contract tests and changelogs that never break live integrations.
* Webhook Delivery at Scale - Design and operate webhooks with HMAC signing, replay protection, retries with backoff, dead-letter handling, ordering guarantees and consumer back-pressure.
* Event-Driven Systems - Design and run Kafka flows: partitioning, ordering, idempotent consumers, retries, dead-letter handling and consumer lag.
* App Lifecycle - Own registration, review, publish, install and uninstall, and the data and permissions each transition must leave behind.
* Multi-Tenant Database Performance - Drive tenant-scoped queries, tenant-leading indexes, partitioning and safe expand-then-contract migrations.
* Caching & Rate Limiting - Use Redis deliberately for caching, distributed locking and per-app / per-merchant rate limiting.
* Production Reliability - Own SLOs and alerts, on-call and incident response, root-cause analysis with observability and APM tooling, and lasting fixes.
* AI-Ready Platform - Design APIs and tool definitions (for example, MCP servers) that LLM agents can use safely, with scoped permissions, rate limits and abuse controls.
* AI Developer Experience - Build LLM-backed features where they help, such as app-review assistance, docs search or integration debugging, with evals and guardrails.
* Reviews & Mentoring - Review critical changes, mentor SDE 1 engineers, and use AI tools across the loop while verifying everything they produce.

**Who You Are**

* 3+ years of backend engineering with strong Node.js and TypeScript, with hands-on ownership of production services.
* Strong low-level design and working high-level design: you explain constraints, choose an approach and make accountable decisions.
* Multi-tenant data isolation in practice: tenant scoping on every query, cache key, job and webhook, and how to prevent and detect cross-tenant leaks.
* Deep relational database skills (MySQL / PostgreSQL): data modelling, transactions and isolation, indexing, reading query plans and fixing slow queries at scale.
* Designed and shipped APIs consumed by external parties, including versioning, deprecation and backward compatibility.
* Production experience with OAuth 2.0 or similar token-based authorisation, and a security mindset around tokens, scopes and secrets.
* Hands-on Kafka or a similar broker: consumer groups, ordering, at-least-once delivery, idempotency, dead-letter queues and lag monitoring.
* Distributed-systems fundamentals: idempotency, retries and backoff, rate limiting, backpressure and consistency trade-offs.
* Real production ownership: on-call, debugging live incidents, root-cause analysis, and monitoring with logs, metrics and traces.
* Solid understanding of LLM systems: tool/function calling, RAG and vector search, evals, guardrails, prompt injection, and the security implications of letting AI agents call platform APIs.
* Uses AI coding tools daily and productively, with the judgement to verify, test and own generated code.
* Clear design documentation and technical communication, with experience reviewing others' work and mentoring.
* Treats an external contract as a promise and plans its change before it is needed; writes down the failure mode, such as what happens if a process crashes between the API call and the commit.
* Leads with data, acts early without waiting to be asked, and owns outcomes beyond your own tickets.

**Why GoKwik**
At GoKwik, you work on large-scale commerce infrastructure where correctness under failure, performance at scale, and code the next engineer can change safely all matter. The App Store & Developer Platform is how third-party developers extend GoKwik for merchants, so your work shapes an ecosystem that other products depend on.
  
  
You get high ownership of design and production systems, real distributed-systems problems, and the chance to make a platform safe for AI agents and AI-built apps. We use AI across how we build while keeping full responsibility for what ships, in a collaborative, engineering-led environment with strong career growth potential.

title: Software Development Engineer I (Backend)
description:
**About GoKwik**
GoKwik is India’s leading D2C Commerce Growth Platform, helping 15,000+ brands acquire, convert, engage, and retain shoppers. Powered by a network of 200M+ shoppers, 500M+ checkouts, and 1.5B+ customer conversations, we’re building the operating system for commerce growth.
  
  
Why This Role Matters
  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer I to build and maintain backend services for GoKwik’s commerce platform. The platform supports multiple merchants, handles large volumes of API traffic, and integrates with external systems and third-party applications.
  
  
In this role, you will develop backend features using Node.js and TypeScript, work with SQL databases and APIs, and contribute to the reliability, performance, and scalability of production systems. You will own small-to-medium features end to end, from design and development to testing, deployment, and post-release monitoring, with guidance from senior engineers.
  
  
The role also requires the effective use of AI-assisted development tools to improve engineering productivity while maintaining code quality, security, and reliability.
  
  
What You’ll Own
  
  

* Backend Development: Design, develop, test, and maintain backend services and REST APIs using Node.js and TypeScript.
* Feature Ownership: Take ownership of small-to-medium features from initial design and data modelling through implementation, testing, rollout, and post-release monitoring.
* API Design and Development: Build REST APIs with appropriate validation, error handling, pagination, status codes, and idempotent write operations.
* Database Design and Optimisation: Write efficient SQL queries, work with indexes and data models, analyse query execution plans, and identify opportunities to improve database performance.
* Multi-Tenant Data Management: Ensure that database queries, cache keys, APIs, and background jobs correctly scope data to the relevant merchant and maintain data isolation.
* Database Migrations: Implement schema changes and database migrations with guidance from senior engineers, ensuring safe execution and rollback options in production environments.
* Integrations and Background Processing: Develop third-party integrations and background jobs that handle retries, timeouts, API rate limits, and partial failures. Use queues and Redis where appropriate.
* Caching and Idempotency: Apply caching, queuing, and idempotency patterns to improve performance and ensure reliable processing when requests or jobs are retried.
* Production Monitoring and Debugging: Add structured logs, metrics, and traces to new code paths. Use application performance monitoring tools to investigate production issues and document root causes.
* AI-Assisted Development: Use AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot for design, coding, testing, code review, and debugging. Validate generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability before deployment.
* AI and LLM-Based Features: Contribute to LLM-powered features, including prompt design, structured outputs, and tool calling, with guidance from senior engineers where required.
* Code Reviews and Collaboration: Review code, incorporate feedback, document technical decisions, and collaborate with other engineers to maintain code quality and engineering standards.

Who You Are
  
  

* Have 1–3 years of experience building production backend services using Node.js and TypeScript, including experience shipping and supporting at least one feature in production.
* Have a sound understanding of data structures, algorithms, problem-solving, and debugging fundamentals.
* Are comfortable writing SQL queries, using joins and indexes, reading query execution plans, and investigating slow queries.
* Understand multi-tenant architecture and the importance of correctly isolating merchant data across queries, caches, and background jobs.
* Have a practical understanding of caching, queues, retries, and idempotency, including how systems behave when requests fail or jobs execute more than once.
* Understand REST API design principles, including request validation, status codes, pagination, error handling, and idempotent writes.
* Use AI coding tools regularly and can evaluate generated code for correctness, security, test coverage, and maintainability.
* Have strong written communication skills and can document technical designs, pull requests, implementation decisions, and incident summaries.
* Take ownership of assigned features, communicate blockers early, seek clarification when requirements are ambiguous, and follow through after release.
* Are open to feedback, willing to learn from senior engineers, and committed to continuously improving your technical skills.

Why GoKwik
  
  
At GoKwik, you will work on production commerce infrastructure that supports a growing ecosystem of D2C brands. You will gain hands-on experience building backend services, working with multi-tenant systems, and solving practical challenges in database performance, integrations, and production reliability. With guidance from experienced engineers, you will own features end to end, develop your system design skills, and learn to use AI-assisted engineering tools responsibly in a production environment.

title: Software Development Engineer III (Frontend)
description:
**About GoKwik**
GoKwik is a growth operating system for D2C and eCommerce brands, enabling checkout optimization, RTO reduction, payments, retention, and post-purchase engagement. Today, GoKwik powers 15,000+ merchants globally, processes ~$2 billion in GMV, and continues to strengthen its AI-powered infrastructure across India, the UK, Europe, and the US.
  
  
Why This Role Matters
  
  
As a Senior Frontend Engineer on the Internal Admin Platform, you will own the console that GoKwik's operations, support and partner-management teams use every day to manage merchant accounts, applications, permissions and configuration. Our platform is multi-tenant: one system serves thousands of merchants, each with its own catalogue, orders, inventory, pricing and customers, and it handles millions of API calls every week. A developer ecosystem sits on top, where third parties build and publish apps that extend what merchants can do.
  
  
This is production engineering, not greenfield prototyping. The services you join already carry live traffic, real merchant data and third-party integrations that cannot break. The role owns architecture, not only screens: frontend conventions, performance budgets, role-based access across UI and API, and the backend endpoints the console depends on. Getting access control or merchant data scoping wrong is a security issue, not a UI bug.
  
  
The console is a React + TypeScript single-page app on Vite, built on a shared component library, with server state in TanStack Query and every form validated through Zod. An older shell still runs on a micro-frontend host with Redux and a different component library, and you will lead the move from one to the other. Where AI genuinely helps operators, such as search, summarisation or assisted triage, you will bring it into the console and design it so a human stays in control of its output.
  
  
What You'll Own
  
  

* Frontend Architecture - Own module boundaries, shared component and hook patterns, state ownership, and the conventions other engineers build on.
* Complex Admin Workflows - Build large data tables, server-side filtering, multi-step forms, bulk actions and audit-friendly detail views in React + TypeScript.
* Server State - Own server state end to end with TanStack Query: cache-key design, invalidation after writes, optimistic updates with rollback, and correct loading, empty, error and permission-denied states.
* Role-Based Access (RBAC) - Design and enforce access across UI and API, so permission rules are defined once, verified on the backend and tested in both places.
* Merchant Data Scoping - Ensure every screen, query and cache key is scoped to the right merchant, so one merchant's data never appears in another's view.
* Legacy Migration - Lead the incremental move from the legacy micro-frontend shell (Redux, older component library) to the modern Vite stack without breaking live users.
* Performance at Scale - Set and hold budgets for bundle size, code-splitting, virtualised rendering and measured interaction latency at real data volumes.
* Backend Endpoints - Design and build the Node.js + TypeScript endpoints your screens need, including validation, pagination, query shape and indexes.
* AI-Assisted Features - Build AI features where they help operators, with streaming UI, structured outputs, guardrails and clear failure states.
* Quality & Reviews - Write component, hook and end-to-end tests (Vitest/Jest, Testing Library, Playwright), review others' frontend changes substantively, and use AI coding tools while verifying what they generate.

Who You Are
  
  

* 4–6 years building production React applications in TypeScript, including ownership of a large or long-lived codebase.
* Deep React knowledge: rendering and reconciliation, memoisation trade-offs, concurrent features, and diagnosing re-renders with the profiler.
* Strong server-state design with TanStack Query or equivalent: cache keys, invalidation, optimistic updates and consistency after mutations.
* Hands-on with schema-driven forms (react-hook-form + Zod or equivalent) and a utility-CSS / headless-component stack (Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Radix or similar).
* Proven frontend performance work at scale: code-splitting, virtualisation, bundle analysis and interaction latency.
* Has implemented RBAC or permission-gated UI, and understands why the backend must remain the source of truth.
* Understands multi-tenant data discipline: every view, request and cache key must be scoped to the right merchant.
* Enough backend to own an endpoint: Node.js, REST design, validation, SQL and indexes.
* Uses AI coding tools daily and productively, with the judgement to catch generated code that is incorrect, insecure or untested.
* Testing discipline across unit, integration and end-to-end tests, focused on behaviour rather than implementation.
* Designs the empty, loading, error and permission-denied states, not only the happy path, and thinks about what a screen does when the API is slow or returns half the data.
* Improves older code incrementally, argues for rewrites with data, and raises the bar for others through reviews and conventions.

Why GoKwik
  
  
At GoKwik, you work on large-scale commerce infrastructure where correctness under failure, performance at scale, and code the next engineer can change safely all matter. The Internal Admin Platform is the control centre for the teams that keep thousands of merchants running, so your work directly shapes how GoKwik operates every day.
  
  
You get high ownership of architecture and conventions, a modern stack, a meaningful migration to lead, and the chance to bring AI into an operator-facing product in a responsible way. We use AI across how we build while keeping full responsibility for what ships, in a collaborative, engineering-led environment with strong career growth potential.

* Design & Delivery - Own the design and delivery of app-store and developer-platform services: write low-level and high-level designs, decide on APIs, data models and failure handling, and document the reasoning.
* OAuth & Token Lifecycle - Own OAuth 2.0 flows end to end: authorisation code with PKCE, refresh and rotation, revocation, scope enforcement and the failure modes of each.
* Public APIs - Build and version public APIs that external developers integrate against, with deprecation paths, contract tests and changelogs that never break live integrations.
* Webhook Delivery at Scale - Design and operate webhooks with HMAC signing, replay protection, retries with backoff, dead-letter handling, ordering guarantees and consumer back-pressure.
* Event-Driven Systems - Design and run Kafka flows: partitioning, ordering, idempotent consumers, retries, dead-letter handling and consumer lag.
* App Lifecycle - Own registration, review, publish, install and uninstall, and the data and permissions each transition must leave behind.
* Multi-Tenant Database Performance - Drive tenant-scoped queries, tenant-leading indexes, partitioning and safe expand-then-contract migrations.
* Caching & Rate Limiting - Use Redis deliberately for caching, distributed locking and per-app / per-merchant rate limiting.
* Production Reliability - Own SLOs and alerts, on-call and incident response, root-cause analysis with observability and APM tooling, and lasting fixes.
* AI-Ready Platform - Design APIs and tool definitions (for example, MCP servers) that LLM agents can use safely, with scoped permissions, rate limits and abuse controls.
* AI Developer Experience - Build LLM-backed features where they help, such as app-review assistance, docs search or integration debugging, with evals and guardrails.
* Reviews & Mentoring - Review critical changes, mentor SDE 1 engineers, and use AI tools across the loop while verifying everything they produce.
